{{2026 Winter Olympics}}
The [[2026 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the XXV Winter Olympic Games, were an international winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Milan]] and [[Cortina d'Ampezzo]], Italy, from 6 to 22 February. A total of 2,900 athletes representing 92 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated,<ref>{{cite web |title=Milano Cortina 2026 Olympic Athletes – Biographies, Medals & More |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results/hubs/individuals/athletes |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |archive-date=16 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260216144917/https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results/hubs/individuals/athletes |url-status=dead }}</ref> including first-time entrants [[Benin at the 2026 Winter Olympics|Benin]], [[Guinea-Bissau at the 2026 Winter Olympics|Guinea-Bissau]], and the [[United Arab Emirates at the 2026 Winter Olympics|United Arab Emirates]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rhys |first1=Paul |title=Winter Olympics 2026: Benin's flagbearer Nathan Tchibozo hopes to begin path to greatness in Bormio |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/news/winter-olympics-2026-benin-flagbearer-nathan-tchibozo-path-to-greatness-bormio |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |date=February 13, 2026}}{{dead link|date=September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Guinea-Bissau makes Winter Olympics debut with teen skier Tang |url=https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260213-guinea-bissau-makes-winter-olympics-debut-with-teen-skier-winston-tang |website=[[Radio France Internationale]] |date=2026-02-13 |access-date=17 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=UAE makes historic Winter Olympics debut at Milan-Cortina 2026 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/uae-makes-historic-winter-olympics-debut-at-milan-cortina-2026/articleshow/128022596.cms |website=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |date=7 February 2026 |archive-date=8 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208160655/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/uae-makes-historic-winter-olympics-debut-at-milan-cortina-2026/articleshow/128022596.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> The games featured 116 events in eight [[Olympic sports|sports]] across 16 disciplines, including [[ski mountaineering]], which made its Olympic debut.<ref>{{cite web |title=2026 Milan Olympics and Paralympic Games |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/olympics/ |website=[[The Globe and Mail]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |language=en-CA |date=17 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Nottingham |first1=Juliet |title=What is ski mountaineering? A guide to the newest sport at Winter Olympics 2026 |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/news/winter-olympics-2026-an-introduction-to-ski-mountaineering |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |date=February 5, 2026}}{{dead link|date=September 2026}}</ref>

Athletes representing 29 NOCs received at least one medal, with 19 winning at least one gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Milano Cortina 2026 in numbers: record engagement, efficient delivery, world-class performance |url=https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/milano-cortina-2026-in-numbers-record-engagement-efficient-delivery-world-class-performance |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> Athletes from [[Norway at the 2026 Winter Olympics|Norway]] won the most medals overall, with 41, surpassing the previous record of 39 medals set by Norway at the [[2018 Winter Olympics]]. Norwegian athletes also won the most gold medals with 18, breaking the previous record of 16 golds set by the Norwegians at the [[2022 Winter Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Norway wins its 17th gold medal, breaking its record for most golds won in a single Winter Olympics |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/2026/02/20/winter-olympics-norway-gold-record-biathlon/8bd022c6-0e64-11f1-8e91-6e1451aab67e_story.html |date=2026-02-20 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=20 February 2026}}</ref>

[[Brazil at the 2026 Winter Olympics|Brazil]] won the first medal and first gold medal in their Winter Olympic history. It is also the first [[Tropical nations at the Winter Olympics|tropical]], [[Latin America]]n and [[South America]]n National Olympic Committee to win a medal at the Winter Olympics.<ref>{{cite news |title=Winter Olympics 2026: Pinheiro Braathen strikes gold for Brazil's first ever medal – live |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2026/feb/14/winter-olympics-2026-giant-slalom-freestyle-skiing-skeleton-ice-hockey-live?CMP=share_btn_url&page=with%3Ablock-699078598f0893c883d519a8#block-699078598f0893c883d519a8 |date=2026-02-14 |work=[[The Guardian]] |last1=Munday |first1=Billy |last2=Aldred |first2=Tanya |last3=Wallace |first3=James |last4=Munday (now) |first4=Billy |last5=Aldred (earlier) |first5=Tanya |last6=Wallace (later) |first6=James |access-date=14 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Lucas Pinheiro Braathen wins giant slalom gold to secure Brazil's first-ever Winter Olympics medal |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/news/lucas-pinheiro-braathen-wins-giant-slalom-gold-brazil-s-first-ever-winter-olympics-medal |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |date=2026-02-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260214174544/https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/news/lucas-pinheiro-braathen-wins-giant-slalom-gold-brazil-s-first-ever-winter-olympics-medal |archive-date=2026-02-14 |url-status=dead |last1=McAlister |first1=Sean |access-date=14 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Keefer |first1=Zak |date=2026-02-14 |title=Lucas Pinheiro Braathen makes history with gold for Brazil in the men's giant slalom |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7046275/2026/02/14/lucas-pinheiro-braathen-mens-giant-slalom/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260214174849/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7046275/2026/02/14/lucas-pinheiro-braathen-mens-giant-slalom/ |archive-date=14 February 2026 |access-date=14 February 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> [[Georgia at the 2026 Winter Olympics|Georgia]] also won the first medal in their Winter Olympic history.<ref>{{cite news|last=Carroll|first=Rory|date=16 February 2026|title=Figure skating-Metelkina and Berulava win Georgia's first ever Winter Olympic medal|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/figure-skating-metelkina-berulava-win-georgias-first-ever-winter-olympic-medal-2026-02-17/|work=[[Reuters]]|location=London, England|access-date=16 February 2026}}</ref>

Among individual participants, Norwegian [[cross-country skier]] [[Johannes Høsflot Klæbo]] won the most gold and overall medals, with six  medals (all gold).<ref>{{cite web |title=Medallists – Milano Cortina 2026 Bronze, Silver & Gold Medal Winners |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/medals/medallists |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |access-date=23 February 2026}}{{dead link|date=September 2026}}</ref> In doing so, he set the record for the most gold medals won at a single Winter Olympics and most career gold medals won by a Winter Olympic athlete (11 gold medals total).<ref>{{cite web |title=Johannes Høsflot Klæbo becomes 1st athlete to win 6 gold medals at a Winter Games |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/winter/cross-country-skiing/norwegian-klaebo-cross-country-wins-6th-gold-medal-at-one-winter-games-9.7100799 |website=[[CBC.ca]] |date=2026-02-21 |last1=Melley |first1=Brian |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> Among Winter Olympians, Klaebo's 13 overall medals trails only biathlete [[Ole Einar Bjørndalen]] and cross-country skier [[Marit Bjørgen]], the latter of whom holds the record with 15 medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Treacy |first1=Dan |title=Most gold medals in one Winter Olympics: Johannes Hoesflot Klaebo's legendary 2026 breaks all-time record |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/most-gold-medals-one-winter-080002684.html |publisher=Yahoo sports |date=February 21, 2026}}</ref>

==Medals==
{{see also|Olympic medal}}
The official medals of the Games were unveiled in [[Venice]], designed as two halves that symbolise the culmination of an athlete's journey and of all those who have walked beside them along the way. The medals were created by the [[Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato]] (IPZS).<ref>{{cite web |title=Milano Cortina 2026 reveals medals for next year's Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/milano-cortina-2026-reveals-medals-olympic-paralympic-winter-games |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=2025-07-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250726092740/https://www.olympics.com/en/news/milano-cortina-2026-reveals-medals-olympic-paralympic-winter-games |archive-date=2025-07-26 |url-status=live |access-date=15 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Milano Cortina unveil striking medals |url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1154240/milano-cortina-2026-unveils-medals |date=2025-07-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250716112719/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1154240/milano-cortina-2026-unveils-medals |archive-date=2025-07-16 |url-status=live |work=[[Inside the Games]] |last1=Soriano |first1=Daniel}}</ref> They have an essential design that places emotion and teamwork at its core. They feature the traditional Olympic five-ring symbol on one side with an inscription on the reverse that details the event and commemorates the two host cities.<ref>{{cite web |title=A medal-worthy legacy: How the Milan Cortina 2026 medals honor and reinvent Olympic history |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/medal-worthy-legacy-how-milan-cortina-2026-medals-honor-and-reinvent-olympic-history |website=[[NBC Sports]] |date=2025-07-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250719125056/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/medal-worthy-legacy-how-milan-cortina-2026-medals-honor-and-reinvent-olympic-history |archive-date=2025-07-19 |url-status=live |last1=Barrington |first1=Talia |access-date=18 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=2025-07-15 |title=Italy showcases medals for 2026 Winter Games |url=https://www.reuters.com/en/italy-showcases-medals-2026-winter-games-2025-07-15/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250902100715/https://www.reuters.com/en/italy-showcases-medals-2026-winter-games-2025-07-15/ |archive-date=2025-09-02 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

==Medal table==
{{Further|List of 2026 Winter Olympics medal winners}}

The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals. If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref>

===Shared medals===
The following events featured a tie in the medal positions and therefore saw shared medals:

# [[Alpine skiing at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's team combined|Alpine skiing – Men's team combined]] – Shared silver between Austria and Switzerland; no bronze awarded<ref>{{cite web |title=Men's Team Combined Slalom Results – Alpine Skiing &#124; Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics (Feb 6 – 22, 2026) |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results/alp/tc/m/tc----------------/fnl-/0001sl--/race-result |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |access-date=17 February 2026}}{{dead link|date=September 2026}}</ref>
# [[Ski jumping at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's normal hill individual|Ski jumping – Men's normal hill individual]] – Shared bronze between Japan and Switzerland<ref>{{cite web |title=Men's Normal Hill Individual – Final Round Results – Ski Jumping &#124; Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics (Feb 6 – 22, 2026) |url=http://olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results/sjp/in/m/nh----------------/fnl-/0002sj--/result |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=17 February 2026}}</ref>
# [[Alpine skiing at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Women's giant slalom|Alpine skiing – Women's giant slalom]] – Shared silver between Norway and Sweden ([[Sara Hector]] and [[Thea Louise Stjernesund]] had identical times in both runs); no bronze awarded<ref>{{cite web |title=Women's Giant Slalom Run 2 Results – Alpine Skiing &#124; Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics (Feb 6 – 22, 2026) |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results/alp/sl/w/gs----------------/fnl-/000200--/race-result |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |access-date=17 February 2026}}{{dead link|date=September 2026}}</ref>
